column1: # The executable metric-family contract. Tab-separated; lines starting with #
# are comments. One row per family the daemon exports over OTLP — the Rust
# registry test include_str!s this file and grades the registry against it in
# both directions. This file is the SINGLE source of truth for the export —
# docs/architecture/observability.md points here and repeats none of it.
# Transcribed from the retired daemon's registry declarations and now graded
# histogram bounds are in the family's declared unit (the old ms bounds are
# already converted to seconds here, because the Rust side records f64 seconds
#   temporality  delta | cumulative | -   (gauges carry no temporality)
#   policy       fixed:<n> | runner:<n> | shared:cost. A `fixed` ceiling is
#                the PRODUCT of the family's closed label sets and must be at
#                (afd_observability) fails on a row that understates, because a
#                ceiling below the real count makes the SDK fold live series
#                into `otel.metric.overflow` — the backstop that must never fire.
#   labels       comma-joined label keys, or -   (cost families additionally
#                carry the evented attribute keys listed in the trailing
#                # evented-attrs comment; runner families carry runner_id)
#   bounds       comma-joined histogram bucket bounds in `unit`, or -
#   live_read    yes | no   (yes → observable instrument fed by a snapshot)
#   category     latency | traffic | errors | saturation | health (operator legend
#   watch_for    one line of operator guidance — what a change in this family means

column1: # evented-attrs: the cost families' record API may additionally attach these
# keys, bounded by the evented admission layer (never free-form):
# shared:cost declares no series ceiling, and that is deliberate. Every label a
# cost family carries is closed by construction: the evented attrs above are
# enums, and gen_ai.request.model is a vendor-published list. The Zig daemon's
# COST_SERIES_BUDGET = 256 sized a static array in an aggregator hand-rolled
# because Zig has no OpenTelemetry SDK; it was never derived from these rows
# (otel_metrics_families.zig:246 excludes cost families from that arithmetic
# outright). The Rust SDK allocates per stream, so the constraint is gone, and
# a cap here could only fire by folding a real model's spend into an overflow
# bucket — losing the per-model cost attribution these families exist to give.
# The SDK's own 2000-per-stream default remains as a backstop that Dimension
# runner:<n> is the exception, and the only one: runner_id is supplied by the
# customer spinning up runners, so it is bounded by admission or not at all.
